title: SDK integration walkthrough - Atlas Payments
summary: AE + SE walked Atlas Payments through Redwood SDK quickstarts for Python & TypeScript, covered auth (API key vs. short-lived tokens + SSO), environment setup (env vars, docker quickstart), and integration patterns for hosted vs dedicated/private deployments. Security questions around KMS, audit logs and SOC2 were raised. Agreed next steps: share security pack, send pricing/commit options for Dedicated, and schedule a poc benchmark with test dataset.
topics: Auth and secrets management (API keys, KMS, SSO)
Env setup: env vars, Docker, CI setup
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ariana Chen, Marco Diaz (Redwood); Lydia Park, Marcus Bell, Rita Gomez (Atlas Payments)

Summary (auto): quick SDK walkthru, auth, env setup, security questions, poc next steps

[00:00] Ariana: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um I'm Ariana from Redwood, this is Marco, our solutions engineer, we'll run through the SDK quickstarts and then dig into any security or infra questions
[00:12] Lydia: thanks, excited to see how fast we can get this integrated, we're aiming to have a poc in the next 2–3 weeks
[00:18] Marco: cool, we'll keep it practical. I'll start with the python quickstart, show env var setup, the API call pattern, and then switch to TypeScript example
[00:30] Marco: so first off you can install via pip install redwood-inference (note: package name in pip is sometimes redwood-sdk in some tooling, sorry mixup), then set REDWOOD_API_KEY as an env var or use short-lived tokens via our SSO integration
[00:45] Marcus: quick Q — we run CI pipelines and don't want long-lived keys in repo, what's best practice?
[00:52] Marco: yep, totally, we recommend using short-lived tokens minted by your identity provider (OIDC) or our token exchange; store secrets in your CI secret store, or use the KMS-backed signing flow if you're on Private/Dedicated
[01:10] Rita: how does the KMS flow work? we need to know about key rotation and HSM options
[01:20] Marco: for Dedicated/Private you can bring your own KMS/HSM, Redwood supports AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSMs for key wrapping. We store minimal material in our control plane and customer-managed keys are used for at-rest encryption of model inputs if you opt in. I'll follow up with the security doc that has the exact KMS architecture diagram
[01:45] Ariana: jumping back to the SDK, python example looks like: from redwood import Client; client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')); resp = client.generate("Summarize this transaction history") — that pattern maps to TypeScript similar: import { Redwood } from '@redwoodai/sdk' (note: sometimes package name and imports differ between versions)
[02:10] Marcus: are there official quickstart repos we can fork?
[02:15] Marco: yes, we have github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts — python, ts, docker, plus a sample benchmark script. I'll add you to the repo after the call
[02:30] Lydia: on hosted vs dedicated — what are the latency and cost tradeoffs? we care about 99p latency under 200ms for our checkout flows
[02:40] Marco: hosted is easiest to get started and we have verified low-latency models; dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at scale. For 200ms 99p you can either pick a small low-latency model on hosted or provision Dedicated with pinned model variants and CPU/GPU selection tuned for short sequences. We'll recommend a config after we see your traffic profile
[03:05] Marcus: what about prefix/KV cache? our flows are short but many repeated prompts
[03:12] Marco: Redwood's runtime does automatic prefix caching and KV cache reuse across requests; Optimize suggests batching windows and cache policies per route. We'll show an example in the poc script where we enable prefix caching and measure token savings
[03:35] Rita: audit logs and retention — we need 7 years for some compliance, is that doable?
[03:42] Ariana: audit log retention is configurable for Private, and for Dedicated we offer extended retention as an add-on. Hosted has a default retention window but we can discuss extended retention and export options to your SIEM. We'll include details in the security pack
[04:05] Marco: switching to TypeScript snippet: import Redwood from '@redwood/ts'; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); const out = await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-large', messages: [...] }); // quick note: model names vary between catalog versions, we'll send the model mapping spreadsheet
[04:40] Marcus: do we need to pin model versions for reproducibility?
[04:45] Marco: yes, we recommend pinning model versions or model variants in your production routes; Redwood supports rollouts and canary deployments so you can test a new model on a small percentage of traffic before full rollout
[05:05] Lydia: CI deployment example — we'd like a dockerized example that runs the poc locally and in our k8s cluster
[05:12] Marco: we have a docker quickstart that uses an env file and mounts secrets from k8s secret store in the entrypoint; it also includes health checks and telemetry hooks for Redwood Console
[05:28] Ariana: on observability — Console gives token-level cost and latency breakdowns and tracing per route, you can set regression alerts by eval sets
[05:40] Marcus: what's the cheapest way to test high throughput? we don't want to commit to Dedicated yet
[05:45] Marco: you can use hosted with burst capacity for short spikes, or we can spin up a short Dedicated eval pool for the poc — cost options are in the pricing doc I'll share
[06:05] Rita: one more on encryption in flight and at rest
[06:10] Marco: we TLS all traffic in transit, and for at-rest encryption we use customer-managed keys on Private/Dedicated; hosted uses provider-managed KMS by default but you can opt into BYOK for enterprise plans
[06:25] Ariana: ok, let's run through the exact integration steps for your engineers — Marco will demo the python quickstart live and we'll paste the commands in chat
[06:35] Marco: demo time — open terminal, pip install, export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_XXXX, python quickstart.py (note: this is demo key, do not use in prod). The quickstart shows a simple chat/generate call and streaming output example
[07:05] Marcus: streaming looks useful for our UX, any SDK caveats?
[07:10] Marco: streaming via websocket or server-sent events is supported; we have examples for both python and ts. Keep an eye on connection idle timers and sequence length limits which affect memory on the runtime
[07:30] Lydia: we ran a small benchmark with another vendor and had tokenization differences, how do you ensure parity?
[07:38] Marco: tokenization and model variants can cause small diffs; we provide model catalog docs and tokenization artifacts. For poc benchmarking we'll make sure you use the same prompt set and tokenization util so comparisons are apples-to-apples
[07:55] Ariana: I'll send the security pack and model catalog spreadsheet after this call. Marco will prepare a poc benchmark script and a trial API key. Lydia, you'll share the traffic profile and any PII concerns
[08:10] Lydia: yes we'll share a sanitized dataset and our SLA targets
[08:18] Marcus: also include an example of using env secrets in GitHub Actions and in our k8s helm templates
[08:25] Marco: will do, we'll include a sample workflow and helm values
[08:40] Rita: any red flags on regulatory or data residency? we have EU customers so data residency matters for some flows
[08:46] Ariana: Private or Dedicated in EU regions addresses residency; for hosted you can route requests to EU regions and we can provide data processing addenda (DPA) — again this will be in the docs
[09:05] Lydia: what's the timeline if we want a Dedicated eval? we could commit to a short reserved pool for testing
[09:12] Marco: typically we can provision a small Dedicated pool in 1–2 weeks once the contract is signed; for eval we can do shorter-term reserved capacity, I'll include pricing tiers
[09:28] Ariana: recap / next steps: send security pack, pricing, add access to quickstarts repo, provide trial key and poc script, schedule benchmark in two weeks. Any other items?
[09:40] Lydia: that's it from us, thanks everyone
[09:43] Marcus: thanks, looking forward to the poc
[09:45] Ariana: thanks, end call

Notes: transcription contains occasional package name confusions and model catalog name variants; timestamps are approximate. Links discussed: github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts (quickstarts repo), https://redwood.ai/security (security pack placeholder), shared drive link to poc scripts (will be sent)
